title: Angular Modulations in Magnetic Torque Induced by Phase Transitions in the Triangular Supersolid $2H$-AgNiO$_2$
authors: John S. Pearce, Zeyu Ma, Alimamy Bangura, Timo Sorgel, Martin Jansen, Radu Coldea, Amalia I. Coldea
abstract: Easy-axis frustrated triangular lattice antiferromagnets provide an important playground for stabilising a wide range of exotic magnetic phases. The delafossite $2H$-AgNiO$_2$ offers a unique model system containing a lattice of localised ($S=1$) moments surrounded by a honeycomb of itinerant electrons. Below $T_{\rm N} =19$ K, the system exhibits collinear stripe antiferromagnetic order, whereas applied magnetic fields induce a cascade of transitions which has been proposed to contain a magnetic supersolid phase. In this study, we perform detailed angular and field-dependent torque measurements in static fields of up to 45~T on single crystal samples. The angular dependence of the torque displays a sawtooth-shaped signal close to the first supersolid phase, while near $T_{\rm N}$, an unexpected additional modulation emerges. On the other hand, the field dependence of the torque indicates the presence of four field-induced anomalies which evolve in distinct ways as a function of field orientation. To understand these complex behaviours and assess the role of local moments, we employ mean-field and Monte-Carlo calculations on a minimal spin model and construct comprehensive polar phase diagrams at different temperatures. We find that the angular dependence of the torque can be understood in terms of crossing different phase boundaries by field rotation, and we identify qualitative similarities between the experimental and theoretical polar phase diagrams. Our study highlights $2H$-AgNiO$_2$ as a rich anisotropic system that provides a robust example of how spin supersolid orders can manifest in angle-dependent magnetic torque.
summary: This work uses angle- and field-dependent magnetic torque measurements on $2H$-AgNiO$_2$ to map out its complex magnetic phase diagram. By comparing these experimental results with theoretical simulations, the authors confirm the existence of multiple field-induced transitions, providing strong evidence for a magnetic supersolid phase in this anisotropic material.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex magnetic phase transitions, particularly the potential supersolid phase, in the triangular lattice antiferromagnet $2H$-AgNiO$_2$.
main_result: The angular and field-dependent magnetic torque measurements reveal characteristic sawtooth signals and multiple anomalies, which are qualitatively explained by crossing different predicted phase boundaries.
method: The research combines detailed experimental measurements of magnetic torque ($	au$) with theoretical modeling using mean-field and Monte-Carlo simulations on a minimal spin model.
model_or_system: The physical system is the delafossite $2H$-AgNiO$_2$, which features localized $S=1$ moments on a triangular lattice interacting with itinerant electrons. The theory uses a minimal easy-axis $J_1-J_2$ spin model.
key_observables: Magnetic torque ($	au$) as a function of angle ($	heta$) and applied field ($H$), and the identification of multiple field-induced anomalies ($H_1$ to $H_4$).
important_parameters: Critical temperatures ($T_N \approx 19$ K), applied fields up to 45 T, and anisotropy parameters ($D/J_1$).
main_assumptions: The theoretical analysis relies on a minimal spin model and semi-classical approximations, potentially neglecting quadrupolar moments or itinerant electron effects for certain anomalies.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnetic ordering (CAF, SS1, SS2, etc.) and show the evolution of the angular dependence of the torque ($	au$) at various temperatures and fields, highlighting kinks and anomalies corresponding to phase boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by presenting experimental torque measurements across varying fields and angles, correlating the observed anomalies with theoretical phase diagrams constructed via mean-field and Monte-Carlo simulations to map out the complex magnetic phase space.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete, measurable platform (magnetic torque) to probe exotic quantum phases like supersolids in a strongly correlated magnetic insulator, linking macroscopic measurements to microscopic spin models.
